Between September 6, 2026, and October 6, 2026 (the last 30 days), my query returned a total of **4,693** pothole complaints:

- **Pothole in Street Complaint:** 3,591 records
- **Alley Pothole Complaint:** 1,102 records

### Status breakdown
- **Pothole in Street Complaint:**
  - `status: Open` — 2,489
  - `status: Completed` — 1,102
- **Alley Pothole Complaint:**
  - `status: Open` — 859
  - `status: Completed` — 243

### Duplicate flags
The records indicate that out of the 4,693 total requests:
- `duplicate: false` — 2,964
- `duplicate: true` — 1,729

The latest record found in this query has a `created_date` of 2026-10-05T14:29:51.000. You can review the exact query trace and download options below.

q: Who decided to allow a kennel at 111 Pennsylvania Ave, and did anyone vote against it?
answer:
**The kennel was allowed by City Council, and nobody voted against it.**

The record is Ordinance No. 50452, "An Ordinance Granting a Conditional Use Permit to Authorize the Operation of a Kennel on Property Located at 111 Pennsylvania Avenue." It is recorded with status: **Adopted**, status date Aug 25, 2026. The department I see named on it is **Planning**.

Two bodies acted on it:

- **Planning Commission, June 25, 2026** — result: "APPROVAL RECOMMENDED [UNANIMOUS]". Ayes: Kim Sudderth, Scott Bateman, Larry Pendleton, Jeffrey F. Wells, Jake Young, Theresa Whibley. No nays, no abstentions. Lelia Vann is listed as absent.
- **City Council, Aug 25, 2026** — result: "ADOPTED [UNANIMOUS]". Ayes: Kenneth Cooper Alexander, Carlos J. Clanton, Courtney R. Doyle, Mamie B. Johnson, Jeremy D. McGee, John E. Paige, Thomas R. Smigiel Jr., Martin A. Thomas Jr. No nays, no abstentions, no absences listed.

So I found no vote against it in either body — both were unanimous, and the only non-vote is the Planning Commission absence noted above. Both vote records come from minutes marked **draft**, so they can still change.

Two related records on the same parcel and same meetings:

- **Ordinance No. 50451**, a rezoning of the same property (Conditional C-C and PCO-Riverview to Conditional C-C and PCO-Riverview), also adopted Aug 25, 2026 and also unanimous at both bodies. That record notes: "The applicant, Blake Sablatura, 602 E. Bayview Boulevard, was present to answer any questions relative to this matter." The kennel ordinance itself names no applicant.
- Earlier, the city-wide rules for kennels in this overlay district changed: **Ordinance No. 50368** (Council May 19, 2026) amended the zoning table to allow "Kennel" in the PCO-Riverview district by conditional use permit only.

One caution: the city's permit records for 111 Pennsylvania Avenue also show **ZP26-00591**, a zoning permit with status: Pending (application date Feb 27, 2026), and **B26-02679**, a building permit with status: Documents Submitted (applied Sep 22, 2026), with zoning and plan reviews still Pending with due dates in October 2026. Those statuses don't tell me whether the kennel is operating — if you want to know that, the Planning department is the contact I see recorded for the kennel ordinance.

q: How many pothole complaints did Chicago get in the last 30 days?
answer:
I found 4,693 pothole complaints in the 311 data for the 30 days from 2026-09-06 through 2026-10-05, the latest I see in the data.

| Type | Total | Marked duplicate | Not marked duplicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pothole in Street Complaint | 3,591 | 1,363 | 2,228 |
| Alley Pothole Complaint | 1,102 | 366 | 736 |
| **Both** | **4,693** | **1,729** | **2,964** |

The city's 311 data has a "duplicate" flag on each request. If you only want requests not flagged as duplicates, I found 2,964. I don't know how the city decides which requests to flag.

I counted only the two request types with "pothole" in their names. I didn't check whether other request types cover potholes. The latest request I see is from 2026-10-05, so the data may not yet include everything from the last day or so.

The trace below has the exact queries. The CSV download has the full 311 dataset if you want to break the numbers down by ward or by day.

trace.soql: q=pothole 311 service requests
SELECT sr_type, sr_short_code, count(*) AS n WHERE created_date >= '2026-09-06T00:00:00' AND upper(sr_type) LIKE '%POT%' GROUP BY sr_type, sr_short_code LIMIT 100
